title: Can Bees, Dogs Identify Cancer Earlier Than Machines?
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: Researchers at Michigan State University recently found that bees’ sense of “smell” is sensitive enough to identify chemical smells of cancer.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州立大学的研究人员最近发现蜜蜂的 " 烟雾 " 感知到足以识别癌症的化学气味。

sentences.en: Bees sense chemicals in their environment using antennae, structures on their heads, which serve as “noses” to sense smells.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂用天线、头顶结构来感知环境中的化学物质,这些化学物质是用来感知气味的“鼻孔”。

sentences.en: The researchers wrote in a study published last month that honeybees can sniff out lung cancer on a patient’s breath.
sentences.zh: 研究者在上个月发表的一份研究中写道,蜜蜂可以在病人的呼吸中嗅出肺癌。

sentences.en: Debajit Saha is an assistant professor of biomedical engineering at Michigan State University.
sentences.zh: Debajit Saha是密歇根州立大学生物医学工程助理教授。

sentences.en: He was part of a team that published the research.
sentences.zh: 他是一个团队的一部分 出版研究。

sentences.en: “Our world is visual . [The] insects’ world is all based on smell, so their sense of smell is very, very good,” Saha said.
sentences.zh: “我们的世界是视觉的。 昆虫的世界都是以嗅觉为基础的,因此它们的嗅觉非常、非常好。”

sentences.en: “There is quite a bit of research that shows that when some cancer grows inside our body, our breath actually changes.
sentences.zh: “有相当一部分研究表明,当一些癌症在我们体内生长时,我们的呼吸实际上会发生变化。

sentences.en: Our research does show that honeybees can detect lung cancer and possibly other diseases based on the smell of those cells.” Saha and his team placed bees in small harnesses and attached small wires to their brains.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究确实表明,蜜蜂能够检测出这些细胞的气味导致的肺癌和可能的其他疾病。” 萨哈和他的团队将蜜蜂放在小皮带上,并将小丝带绑在他们的大脑上。

sentences.en: The insects were then placed near chemicals that are like the breath of a person with lung cancer.
sentences.zh: 然后这些昆虫被放置在化学物质附近,就像肺癌患者的呼吸一样。

sentences.en: The scientists said that the bees could tell the difference between the cancer breath and the laboratory copy of the healthy human breath 93 percent of the time.
sentences.zh: 科学家们说蜜蜂可以分辨出 癌症的呼吸 和人体健康呼吸的实验室副本 百分之九十三的时间。

sentences.en: The scientists added that the bees could also tell the difference between different kinds of lung cancer.
sentences.zh: 科学家们补充说,蜜蜂也可以分辨出不同种类的肺癌。

sentences.en: The discovery could help doctors detect many cancers, including lung, breast, head and neck, and colorectal cancers, earlier than other methods.
sentences.zh: 这种发现有助于医生比其他方法早发现许多癌症,包括肺癌、乳癌、头癌和颈癌以及直肠癌。

sentences.en: Saha says detecting cancers this way would be an improvement. “The reason is, many times we detect the cancer late,” when a growth has become too big to control easily.
sentences.zh: 萨哈说,通过这种方式检测癌症将是一个进步。 “原因很多次是,我们检测癌症的晚期, ” 当增长变得太大而难以控制的时候。

sentences.en: But, he added, when cancer starts growing the breath starts changing much earlier.
sentences.zh: 但是,他补充说,当癌症开始生长时, 呼吸开始更早地改变。

sentences.en: He hopes to develop a system that a patient will be able to breathe into and which can be carried around easily.
sentences.zh: 他希望开发出一种系统,使病人能够呼吸并轻易携带。

sentences.en: This would deliver test results immediately.
sentences.zh: 这将立即提供测试结果。

sentences.en: “Hopefully, within the next five years, we'll have something to show that humans can be diagnosed using these insect brain disc sensors,” Saha said.
sentences.zh: 萨哈说,“希望在未来五年内,我们将有一些东西表明,人类可以使用这些昆虫脑盘传感器被诊断出来。”

sentences.en: Dogs can also help find cancer Using animals to detect cancer is not a new idea.
sentences.zh: 狗也可以帮助发现癌症 使用动物来检测癌症不是新想法

sentences.en: At the Penn Vet Working Dog Center at the University of Pennsylvania, researchers are training dogs to smell some kinds of cancer.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚大学的Penn Vet工作犬中心,研究人员正在训练狗闻到某种癌症。

sentences.en: Cindy Otto is executive director of the Penn Vet Working Dog Center in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: Cindy Otto是费城Penn Vet工作犬中心的执行主任。

sentences.en: She said many other animals also have very good senses of smell. “But part of what makes dogs so good is that they cooperate with humans, and so, they communicate that information,” she added.
sentences.zh: 她说,许多其他动物也有很好的嗅觉。 “但使狗如此好的部分是它们与人类合作,因此,它们传达了这些信息,”她补充说。

sentences.en: The dogs are in a program where they live with families and are brought to “work” each day.
sentences.zh: 狗与家人一起生活,每天被带去“工作”。

sentences.en: Not all dogs can do this work. Otto said, “They need to love it to be engaged .
sentences.zh: 奥托说,“他们需要爱它才能订婚。

sentences.en: And so, it's a really fun game for them.” Some researchers say that dogs detect cancer better than machines.
sentences.zh: 因此,对于他们来说,这是一个非常有趣的游戏。” 一些研究人员说,狗比机器更能检测癌症。

sentences.en: They note that a dog’s sense of smell is 10,000 to 100,000 times sharper than that of humans.
sentences.zh: 他们指出,狗的嗅觉比人类的嗅觉高一万至十万倍。

sentences.en: Amritha Mallikarjun is another postdoctoral researcher at the center.
sentences.zh: Amritha Mallikarjun是中心的另一个博士后研究员。

sentences.en: She said dogs are more sensitive to smells than any machines sold today.
sentences.zh: 她说狗比今天卖的机器 更敏感

sentences.en: But the scientists hope to create a machine that will identify disease just as well as dogs.
sentences.zh: 但是科学家们希望建立一个机器 能够像狗一样识别疾病

sentences.en: Otto said doctors in ancient Greece and Rome used odor as a tool to identify disease.
sentences.zh: 奥托说古希腊和罗马的医生用气味作为识别疾病的工具。

sentences.en: She hopes the researchers can build on that “and advance the health of not only humans, but dogs and other species as well.” I’m Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 她希望研究人员能够以此为基础,“并且不仅增进人的健康,而且增进狗和其他物种的健康。” 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

sentences.en: Dora Mekouar reported this story for VOA News.
sentences.zh: Dora Mekouar在VOA新闻报导此事,

sentences.zh: 吉尔・罗宾斯改编了它 学习英语。
